scenarios.title: Penalty Against
text: Next match, 70th minute: a penalty against you. The taker is their best player. He always goes to the keeper's right. Always. Doesn't he?
A penalty. The taker is staring at you, trying to read you. You've watched every penalty he has ever taken.

out.text: He goes right. So does {J}. Saved, and held. The stadium explodes.
He goes left for the first time in his career. Goal.

ok.text: He stands until the last moment and gets a strong hand to it. Saved.

bad.text: He waits. The taker waits longer. Goal, rolled into the corner.

scenarios.title: Through on Goal
scenarios.text: Next match: a striker clean through, one-on-one. You have half a second to decide whether to rush out or stay on your line.

choices.label: Rush out and spread
choices.hint: Brave. A foul risks a red.

ok.text: He's out like a shot, spread wide, and the ball hits his knee and loops away. Clean sheet saved.

bad.text: Too late. He clips the striker's ankle. Penalty and a yellow card.

ok.text: The striker shoots early. {J} is perfectly placed. Easy save, made to look easy.

bad.text: The striker takes his time and slots it past him.

scenarios.title: The Last-Minute Corner
scenarios.text: Next match, last minute, a corner against you. Their giant centre-back is in the box. Everyone is looking at you.

ok.text: He rises above everyone and catches it cleanly. Final whistle. Clean sheet.

bad.text: He flaps at it. The ball drops at the giant's feet. Goal.

out.text: The defenders head it clear. Final whistle.
A free header from six yards. Unsaveable. Goal.

scenarios.title: Play It Out
scenarios.text: Next match: the manager wants you to play out from the back under pressure. Their striker is pressing like a madman. Your centre-back is showing for the ball, marked.
scenarios.prompt: What do you do with the ball?

ok.text: A perfect pass through the press starts a counter that ends in a goal. The manager punches the air.

bad.text: Intercepted. Goal. The manager looks at the sky.

choices.label: Kick it long
choices.text: He launches it long. Nothing happens, which is fine.

scenarios.title: The Last Man
scenarios.text: Next match: you're the last defender. Their fastest player is running at you with the ball. If you go to ground and miss, it's a red card.

ok.text: A perfect sliding tackle, all ball. The crowd roars like it's a goal.

bad.text: He catches the man, not the ball. Straight red.

choices.label: Jockey and show him wide
choices.hint: Buys time for help to arrive.

ok.text: He shows the winger down the line until help arrives. Danger over.

bad.text: The winger cuts inside and scores. {J} was too passive.

scenarios.title: Set-Piece Target
scenarios.text: Next match: a corner for you, late on. The coach has drawn your name in a circle on the set-piece sheet. You're the target.
scenarios.prompt: How do you attack the corner?

ok.text: He meets it at the near post and glances it into the far corner. A centre-back's goal.

bad.text: Mistimed. The ball skims off his head and out for a goal kick.

choices.label: Block the keeper, free a teammate
choices.text: He blocks the keeper's path and {CAPl} heads it in. Nobody notices {J}'s role except the coach.

scenarios.title: Step Into Midfield
scenarios.text: Next match: their midfield keeps dropping off. There's space in front of you, acres of it. The coach has told you to step in when you see it.

choices.label: Carry it forward and split them with a pass

ok.text: He strides into midfield and threads a pass between two lines. Assist.

bad.text: He loses it and they counter into the space he left behind. Goal.

choices.label: Keep it simple
choices.text: Simple and safe, all match. The coach wanted more. The clean sheet didn't.

scenarios.title: The Overlap
scenarios.text: Next match: the winger in front of you has the ball and nobody is tracking your run. Bomb on, or stay home and protect?

choices.label: Sprint the overlap and cross
choices.hint: Assist, or caught out of position.

ok.text: He hits the byline and whips in a cross. The striker can't miss. Assist.

bad.text: The cross is cut out and they break down his empty flank. Goal.

choices.label: Hold your position
choices.text: He stays home. Their counter-attacks die on his flank all match.

scenarios.title: The Fastest Man in the League
scenarios.text: Next match, you're up against the league's fastest winger. He's beaten every full-back he's faced this season. The whole match is this duel.

choices.label: Stand off and use your body

ok.text: He never gives him a yard. The winger is subbed in the 60th minute, furious.

bad.text: One burst of pace and he's gone. Cross, goal.

ok.text: Two crunching early challenges, both fair. The winger disappears from the game.

bad.text: Yellow card after eight minutes. He spends the rest of the match on a tightrope.

scenarios.title: Their Number Ten
scenarios.text: Next match: their playmaker floats between the lines and kills teams. Your job is to make sure he never turns.

ok.text: The playmaker touches the ball eleven times all match. The coach calls it the perfect defensive display.

bad.text: He drags {J} out of position and a teammate exploits the hole. Goal.

choices.label: Break up play with a tactical foul
choices.text: Three tactical fouls, one yellow, zero counter-attacks. The cynical art.

scenarios.title: Room to Shoot
scenarios.text: Next match: their defence keeps dropping deep. You'll get space thirty yards out. Nobody ever closes down the holding midfielder.

choices.label: Let fly
choices.hint: Goal of the season, or row Z.

ok.text: It swerves, dips and kisses the underside of the bar on the way in. Goal of the season.

bad.text: Row Z. The fans behind the goal throw it back.

choices.label: Recycle it
choices.text: He keeps it simple and moves it on. Ninety-four per cent pass accuracy.

scenarios.title: The Pass Nobody Sees
scenarios.text: Next match: there's a gap between their centre-backs that opens for half a second every time their striker presses. Your striker has noticed too.

ok.text: The gap opens and the ball is already through it. One-on-one, goal. Assist.

bad.text: Intercepted and countered. The coach throws his water bottle.

choices.label: Control the tempo
choices.text: He dictates the rhythm all match. The team wins the possession battle, if not the highlights reel.

scenarios.title: Late Run
scenarios.text: Next match: when the winger gets to the byline, nobody is ever arriving at the edge of the box. That could be you, if your legs allow it.
scenarios.prompt: Make the late run into the box?

choices.label: Arrive late at the edge
choices.hint: A goal if the cut-back comes.

ok.text: The cut-back comes, he arrives on time, side-foot finish. Goal.

bad.text: He's a step too late every time, and too tired to track back for their goal.

choices.label: Stay in your lane
choices.text: He stays in position all match. Disciplined, unspectacular, important.

scenarios.title: Free Kick, Twenty-Two Yards
scenarios.text: Next match: a free kick just outside the box. The regular taker is injured. Everybody looks at {J}.

ok.text: Over the wall, under the bar. The keeper doesn't move.

bad.text: Straight into the wall. The rebound is cleared.

out.text: The routine works perfectly. Goal, and an assist.
The routine goes wrong. Nobody knows who was supposed to run where.

scenarios.title: Between the Lines
scenarios.text: Next match: their holding midfielder is slow to turn. If you can receive on the half-turn, you're facing goal with space.
scenarios.prompt: Take the risk of receiving under pressure?

ok.text: He spins his marker, drives forward and slides it home. Goal.

bad.text: He's caught on the turn and they break. {Mf} is not impressed.

choices.label: Lay it off first time
choices.text: One-touch football all afternoon. Good, not great.

scenarios.title: Isolated Against the Full-Back
scenarios.text: Next match: their right-back is on a yellow card and slow on the turn. You'll get him one-on-one at least five times.

choices.label: Take him on every time
choices.hint: He'll be sent off or you'll be brilliant.

ok.text: He destroys the full-back. A cut inside, a curled finish. Goal.

bad.text: The full-back reads him every time. A frustrating afternoon.

choices.label: Get to the byline and cross

ok.text: Byline, cut-back, goal. Assist.

bad.text: Every cross finds the first defender.

scenarios.title: The Counter-Attack
scenarios.text: Next match: they will commit everyone to their corners. If you stay up the pitch, you'll be running at a back line of one.

choices.label: Stay up and run
choices.hint: A goal, or you're blamed for their header.

ok.text: The clearance falls to him at halfway. Sixty yards, one defender, goal.

bad.text: He stays up. They score from the corner because the man he should have marked was free.

choices.label: Defend the corner
choices.text: He tracks back for every corner. Unglamorous. The manager notices.

scenarios.title: Cross Incoming
scenarios.text: Next match: their centre-backs struggle in the air. The winger will cross all day. Near post or far post?
scenarios.prompt: Where do you attack the cross?

ok.text: He gets in front of his marker and flicks it in at the near post. Goal.

bad.text: Beaten to it every time.

ok.text: He drifts away unnoticed and the cross finds him alone. Easy header. Goal.

bad.text: The crosses never reach the far post.

scenarios.title: The Keeper Comes Out
scenarios.text: Next match: their keeper rushes off his line at everything. One-on-one, he'll be on you in a flash.
scenarios.prompt: How do you beat a rushing keeper?

ok.text: The softest touch, over the diving keeper, into the empty net. Pure art.

bad.text: The chip lands on the roof of the net. The keeper laughs.

choices.label: Round him
choices.desc: Go past and walk it in.

ok.text: He drops a shoulder, rounds the keeper and walks it in.

bad.text: Taken too wide. A defender clears off the line.

scenarios.title: Penalty Duty
scenarios.text: Next match: the regular penalty taker is out. The coach has asked who wants it if the moment comes. Nobody answered. Then everyone looked at you.

ok.text: A penalty in the 80th minute. Stuttered run-up, keeper the wrong way. Goal.

bad.text: He hits the post. The silence is deafening.

choices.label: Let the captain take it
choices.text: The captain takes it and scores. {J} is first to celebrate with him.

scenarios.title: Back to Goal
scenarios.text: Next match: the team will play long to you all game. Their centre-back is huge and enjoys hurting strikers.
scenarios.prompt: How do you play against him?

ok.text: He wins every duel. The centre-back is subbed at half-time with a sore ego. {J} sets up the winner.

bad.text: He's bullied all afternoon and limps off late on.

ok.text: He spins in behind every time. The big man can't turn. Goal.

bad.text: Offside, offside, offside.

scenarios.title: A Touch in the Box
scenarios.text: Next match: in the box, a defender will brush your shoulder. Not a foul. Not quite. But if you go down...

choices.label: Stay on your feet
choices.text: He stays up and shoots. Saved. A commentator praises his honesty.

choices.label: Go down
choices.hint: Penalty or a yellow for diving.

out.text: Penalty. Converted. The replays are not kind.
Yellow card for simulation. The away fans chant about it for the rest of the match.

scenarios.title: Something Pulls
scenarios.text: Next match, thirty minutes in, you'll feel something pull in your thigh. Not agony. A warning.

choices.label: Signal to come off
choices.text: He signals to the bench and comes off. The scan shows a tiny strain, caught early.

out.text: It loosens up. He plays the full ninety.
In the 70th minute, it goes. Properly.

scenarios.title: Provoked
scenarios.text: Next match: their midfielder will spend the whole game insulting your family, stamping on your heels and laughing. He wants you sent off.
scenarios.prompt: How do you keep your head?

ok.text: He doesn't react once. In the 85th minute the midfielder loses it himself and gets sent off.

bad.text: In the 60th minute, he snaps and shoves him. Straight red.

choices.label: Ask the referee to watch him
choices.text: The referee watches closely and books the midfielder. The provocation stops.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Armband
scenarios.text: Next match: the referee will make a terrible decision against you early, and your teammates will lose their heads. As captain, it's on you to calm them.

ok.text: He pulls the team into a huddle. Ten seconds, three sentences. They come back stronger.

bad.text: Nobody listens. Two teammates are booked for dissent within five minutes.

choices.label: Argue with the referee yourself
choices.text: He argues fiercely and gets a yellow card. His team loves him for it. The referee doesn't.

scenarios.title: Big Stadium, Small Boy
scenarios.text: Next match: the biggest crowd you've ever played in front of. Forty thousand people. Your legs feel like they belong to someone else.
scenarios.prompt: How do you handle the nerves?

choices.label: Keep it simple at the start
choices.text: Five simple passes and the nerves fade. By the second half he's enjoying himself.

out.text: A rainbow flick in the third minute. The crowd gasps. He's arrived.
The rainbow flick hits his own heel. Forty thousand people laugh at once.

scenarios.title: The Young Legs
scenarios.text: Next match: you'll be up against a nineteen-year-old who runs like the wind and doesn't know who you are. Your legs aren't what they were.
scenarios.prompt: How does the old head handle the young legs?

ok.text: He's always one step ahead without ever running. The kid asks for his shirt at full time.

bad.text: The kid is simply too quick. A tough afternoon.

choices.label: Ask for a role with less running
choices.text: The coach shifts him into a quieter role. He's useful, if not spectacular.

scenarios.title: If You Score Against Them
scenarios.text: Next match: {R}. If you score, you'll be running towards their fans, who have been abusing you for ninety minutes.
scenarios.prompt: If you score, how do you celebrate?

out.text: He scores and stands in front of them with a hand to his ear. Yellow card, legendary photo.
He doesn't score. Their fans sing about it for an hour.
He scores and sprints to his own fans. A pile-on of joy.
No goal today. He still applauds his fans at the end.

scenarios.title: Waterlogged
scenarios.text: Next match: torrential rain is forecast. The ball will stop dead in puddles. Pretty football will be impossible.

choices.label: Play direct
choices.text: He adapts first. The team plays in the air and wins every second ball. Ugly, effective.

out.text: One perfect pass skims across a puddle into the striker's path. Assist.
The ball dies in a puddle and they counter. Goal.

scenarios.title: Thirty-Six Degrees
scenarios.text: Next match kicks off at 3pm in thirty-six degrees and ninety per cent humidity. Even the referee looks worried.
scenarios.prompt: How do you manage your energy?

choices.label: Pace yourself
choices.text: He walks when he can and sprints when it matters. In the last ten minutes he's the only one still running.

choices.label: Go flat out from the start

out.text: An early blitz, an early goal. Then cramp.
He's empty by the 50th minute and subbed.

scenarios.title: Out of Position
scenarios.text: Next match: injuries everywhere. The manager wants you to play a position you've never played. Just for this match.
scenarios.prompt: Agree to play out of position?

out.text: He's surprisingly good there. The manager is quietly impressed.
He's lost all match but never stops running. The manager thanks him anyway.

choices.label: Ask to stay in your role
choices.text: The manager shuffles someone else. He notes who said no.

scenarios.title: {MUM} Is Coming
scenarios.text: Next match: {MUM} is coming to watch for the first time in a year. She's made a banner. It's very large and has his baby photo on it.
scenarios.prompt: Will it inspire you, or distract you?

choices.label: Play for her
choices.text: He plays the match of his life and runs to the banner at full time. {MUM} is in tears.

choices.label: Ask her to bring a smaller banner
choices.text: She brings a bigger banner. He plays fine and pretends not to see it.

scenarios.title: Ninety-Fourth Minute
scenarios.text: Next match: 1-1, ninety-fourth minute, the ball will drop to you twenty yards out. Shoot, or pass to the teammate in a better position?

ok.text: He hits it sweet. Top corner. The stadium loses its mind.

bad.text: Over the bar. His teammate, who was in on goal, throws his arms up.

out.text: Perfect pass, simple finish. Winner. Assist.
His teammate misses an open goal. {J} stares at the sky.

scenarios.title: The Ball Over the Top
scenarios.text: Next match: their striker will chase a ball over the top. You could race out of your box and clear it, or stay home and wait.

ok.text: He's out like a flash and heads it clear thirty yards from goal. The crowd gasps, then applauds.

bad.text: He misjudges it. The striker rounds him into an empty net.

ok.text: The striker shoots early. Saved.

bad.text: He finishes coolly. Goal.

scenarios.title: Step Up
scenarios.text: Next match: as the organiser of the back line, it's your call when to step up for offside. Their striker loves running on the shoulder.

ok.text: Five offsides in the first half. The striker is furious. Clean sheet.

bad.text: Mistimed once. Once is enough. Goal.

choices.label: Drop deep
choices.text: He drops deep. They dominate possession and do nothing with it.

scenarios.title: Protect the Lead
scenarios.text: Next match: if you're 1-0 up with fifteen minutes left, the manager wants you to drop between the centre-backs and see it out.
scenarios.prompt: How do you see the game out?

ok.text: He blocks four shots in fifteen minutes. The lead holds.

bad.text: A deflection off his own leg loops in. 1-1.

ok.text: He keeps the ball for most of the last fifteen minutes. The opposition never touch it.

bad.text: Caught in possession. Equaliser.

scenarios.title: Track Back or Stay High
scenarios.text: Next match: their full-back bombs forward constantly. The manager wants you to track him all the way. Your legs want to stay high.

choices.label: Track him every time
choices.text: He tracks every run. Exhausted, unglamorous, important. The manager mentions it in the press conference.

out.text: Their full-back stops bombing on because he's scared of {J}. Problem solved by threat.
The full-back keeps coming. Cross, goal. The manager's face says everything.

scenarios.title: The Big Stage
scenarios.text: Next match is the biggest of the season. The whole country is watching. Your phone hasn't stopped buzzing all week.

choices.label: Phone off all week
choices.text: Phone in a drawer, early nights, visualisation. On the day he's calm and sharp.

out.text: The buzz carries him. He plays like a man possessed.
The buzz becomes noise. He's flat and distracted.

scenarios.title: {T} Goes Down
scenarios.text: Next match: early on, {T} will go down badly near you. He'll be in real pain. The ball is still in play.

choices.label: Kick it out immediately
choices.text: He kicks it out without thinking. {T} is stretchered off with a thumbs up. Both sets of fans applaud.

choices.label: Play on
choices.text: He plays on, and they score from the move. Some fans aren't happy about it.
